text:
maya: Heads up — I'm seeing the scrape-proxy queue in us-west1 climb and a burst of remote_write 5xxs. p95 write latency jumped to ~4s at 21:04 UTC. Anyone else?
jon: yup same. grafana: https://grafana.redwood.com/d/abcd/scrape-proxy?orgId=1 time range now shows backlog spike :grimacing: 
maya: oncall-bot just opened INC-4821 for the alert.
oncall-bot: Incident INC-4821 - scrape-proxy write_latency_p95 breached in us-west1 (started 21:03 UTC).
alejandro: logs from the proxy show a bunch of TLS handshake timeouts to remote-write endpoints, and the local queue is growing: 
alejandro: ```
level=warn ts=2026-03-18T21:03:27.123Z msg="timeout while writing batch" retry=1 err="net/http: TLS handshake timeout" queue_len=1240
```
ivy: interesting — we pushed a relabel change yesterday to keep extra labels, might have increased series cardinality. can someone check the relabel rules?
jon: checking. relabel config for gpu-exporter-stream: 
jon: ```yaml
- source_labels: [__meta_kubernetes_pod_label_pod]
  target_label: pod
- source_labels: [__meta_kubernetes_pod_container_name]
  target_label: container
- action: keep
  regex: gpu.*
```
jon: that keep rule is broad, could be keeping a bunch of ephemeral labels (build ids).
maya: can we temporarily drop the enforce-keep rule and lower write concurrency to throttle?
alejandro: +1 for temp mitigation. we can also increase write timeout from 10s -> 20s to reduce TLS timeouts turning into 5xxs, but that might increase queue.
ivy: quick eval: if we reduce concurrent writers to remote-write from 10->4 it will space out TLS handshakes — less parallel handshake pressure on the endpoint.
jon: I'm flipping the relabel in staging now: changing action: keep -> action: replace with target_label: dropped_by_sre and regex: ^$ to effectively drop ephemeral labels. patch: 
jon: ```diff
- action: keep
- regex: gpu.*
+ action: drop
+ regex: 'build-[0-9]+'
```
jon: applied to canary, scraping looks stable in staging (queue back to normal).
maya: nice. can we also prod remote-write endpoint health? curl returns 200 but times out sporadically.
alejandro: contacted vendor — they're seeing brief TLS renegotiation spikes. they suggest enabling keepalive on the proxy side to reuse TCP/TLS sessions.
ivy: sysctl we use already sets tcp_keepalive_time=120. The proxy's http client might not enable connection reuse aggressively. I can patch to set http.Transport.{MaxIdleConnsPerHost: 100, IdleConnTimeout: 90s} and redeploy a canary.
jon: doing that now in us-west1-canary.
jon: ```bash
kubectl -n monitoring set image deploy/scrape-proxy scrape-proxy=proxy:v2.1.7-canary
```
alejandro: FYI we also hit a cardinality spike on the gpu_exporter:series_count metric correlated with a job that started annotating pods with commit hashes. dropping that label should reduce series churn quickly.
maya: action items so far: 1) jon - roll relabel drop to prod (if canary holds) 2) ivy - deploy http.Transport keepalive patch canary -> prod 3) alejandro - follow up with vendor on TLS reneg negotiation root cause.
jon: canary looks good so far; queue fell from 1.2k -> 80 over 3 minutes. rolling to prod now with 10 min splay.
jon: rolled to prod at 21:12 UTC.
oncall-bot: Alert resolved: write_latency_p95 in us-west1 back under threshold.
maya: great. let's still tune alerting — p95 threshold spike noises when upstream has small blips. maybe require 2m sustained breach and correlate queue_len > 300 before page.
ivy: agree. also add a grafana panel for idle_conn_reuse to confirm keepalive effect.
alejandro: long term: recommend we add a relabel sanity CI that runs daily on a sample cluster config to catch cardinality increases before rollout.
maya: love that. i'll create a follow-up ticket to add relabel CI + alert tuning + a runbook for TLS handshake spikes.
jon: +1. thanks all for rapid responses :thumbsup:
ivy: noted runbook additions: connection reuse, relabel rollback steps, temporary concurrency knob.
maya: closing thread — will post incident summary in #postmortems after we write it up.
